interface.name: zwlr_layer_shell_v1

description.summary: create surfaces that are layers of the desktop

interface.description: Clients can use this interface to assign the surface_layer role to wl_surfaces. Such surfaces are assigned to a "layer" of the output and rendered with a defined z-depth respective to each other. They may also be anchored to the edges and corners of a screen and specify input handling semantics. This interface should be suitable for the implementation of many desktop shell components, and a broad number of other applications that interact with a desktop compositor.

request.name: get_layer_surface

description.summary: create a layer_surface from a surface

request.description:
Create a layer surface for an existing surface. This assigns the role of layer_surface, or raises a protocol error if another role is already assigned.
Creating a layer surface from a wl_surface which has a buffer attached or committed is a client error, and any attempts by a client to attach or commit a buffer prior to the first zwlr_layer_surface_v1.configure event must also be treated as a protocol error.
After creating a layer_surface object and setting it up, the client must perform an initial commit without any buffer attached. The compositor will reply with a zwlr_layer_surface_v1.configure event. The client must acknowledge it and is then allowed to attach a buffer to map the surface.
You may pass NULL for output to allow the compositor to decide which output to use. Generally this will be the one that the user most recently interacted with.
Clients can specify a namespace that defines the purpose of the layer surface.

arg.name: layer
arg.summary: layer to add this surface to

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: wl_surface has a buffer attached or committed

enum.name: layer
enum.description: These values indicate which layers a surface can be rendered in. They are ordered by z depth, bottom-most first. Traditional shell surfaces will typically be rendered between the bottom and top layers. Fullscreen shell surfaces are typically rendered at the top layer. Multiple surfaces can share a single layer, and ordering within a single layer is undefined.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request indicates that the client will not use the layer_shell object any more. Objects that have been created through this instance are not affected.

interface.name: zwlr_layer_surface_v1
interface.description: An interface that may be implemented by a wl_surface, for surfaces that are designed to be rendered as a layer of a desktop region, such as launchers, docks, bar, notifications, etc.

request.name: set_size

description.summary: sets the size of the surface

request.description:
Sets the size of the surface in surface-local coordinates. The compositor will display the surface centered with respect to its anchors.
If you pass 0 for either value, the compositor will assign it and inform you of the assignment in the configure event. You must set your anchor to opposite edges in the dimensions you omit; not doing so is a protocol error. Both values are 0 by default.
Size is double-buffered, see wl_surface.commit.

request.name: set_anchor

description.summary: configures the anchor point of the surface

request.description:
Requests that the compositor anchor the surface to specified edges and corners. If two orthogonal edges are specified (e.g. 'top' and 'left'), then the anchor point will be the intersection of the edges (e.g. the top left corner of the output); otherwise the anchor point will be centered on that edge, or in the center if none is specified.
Anchor is double-buffered, see wl_surface.commit.

request.name: set_exclusive_zone

description.summary: configures the exclusive geometry of this surface

request.description:
Requests that the compositor avoids occluding an area with other surfaces. The compositor's use of this information is compositor-dependent - generally, it's used to prevent maximizing or overlapping windows from configuring themselves into the exclusive zone.
The value is the distance from the anchor edge that should be reserved, in surface-local coordinates. For example, if you're anchored to the top edge and want to reserve 20px for a bar, pass 20.
A positive exclusive zone is only meaningful if the surface is anchored to one edge or an edge and both perpendicular edges. If the surface is not anchored, anchored to only two perpendicular edges (a corner), or anchored to all four edges, its behavior is undefined.
If the exclusive zone is set to -1, the surface indicates that it would like to be left anchored to the edge and not covered by any other surfaces, including other layer surfaces.
If the exclusive zone is set to 0, the surface indicates that it has no desire for an exclusive zone.
The default value is 0.
Exclusive zone is double-buffered, see wl_surface.commit.

request.name: set_margin

description.summary: sets a margin from the anchor edge

request.description:
Requests that the compositor place some distance between the surface and the edges it is anchored to. Negative values are permitted.
Top, right, bottom, and left values are only meaningful if the surface is anchored to that edge.
If the surface is not anchored to any edge, this has no effect.
Margins are double-buffered, see wl_surface.commit.

request.name: set_keyboard_interactivity
request.description:
Set how keyboard events are delivered to this surface. By default, layer shell surfaces do not receive keyboard events; this request can be used to change this.
This setting is inherited by child surfaces set by the get_popup method.
Layer surfaces receive pointer, touch, and tablet events normally. If you do not want to receive them, set the input region on your wl_surface to an empty region.
Keyboard interactivity is double-buffered, see wl_surface.commit.

request.name: get_popup

description.summary: assign this layer_surface as an xdg_popup parent

request.description:
This assigns an xdg_popup's parent to this layer_surface. This must have been previously set as a layer surface via get_layer_surface.
The parent must be mapped, or protocol error is raised.
This request assigns the parent of popup. It must be followed by a commit on the popup surface to take effect.

request.name: ack_configure
request.description:
When a configure event is received, if a client commits the surface in response to the configure event, then the client must make an ack_configure request sometime before the commit request, passing along the serial of the configure event.
For instance, for the width and height fields, the client will acknowledge a configure event by sending the ack_configure request before committing a buffer of the appropriate size.
If the client receives multiple configure events before it can respond to one, it only has to ack the latest configure event.
A client is not required to commit immediately after sending an ack_configure request - it may even ack multiple configure events before committing a buffer.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: the serial from the configure event

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request destroys the layer surface and removes the layer surface from the screen. This is a double-buffered operation, and the surface is removed upon the next wl_surface.commit.

event.name: configure
event.description:
The configure event asks the client to resize its surface.
Clients should arrange their surface for the new states, and then send an ack_configure request with the serial sent in this event at some point before committing the new surface.
The client is free to dismiss all but the last configure event it received.
The width and height arguments specify the size of the surface in surface-local coordinates.
The size is a hint, in the sense that the client is free to ignore it if it doesn't resize, pick a smaller size (if it doesn't want to), or pick a larger size. However, the client should always respect the size and position of the surface as set by the compositor.
If the width or height arguments are 0, it means the client should decide its own width or height.

event.name: closed
event.description:
The closed event is sent by the compositor when the surface will no longer be shown. The output may have been destroyed or the user may have called the compositor's destructor.
The client is expected to destroy the zwlr_layer_surface_v1 object and the associated wl_surface.

entry.name: top
entry.summary: the top edge of the anchor rectangle

entry.name: bottom
entry.summary: the bottom edge of the anchor rectangle

entry.name: left
entry.summary: the left edge of the anchor rectangle

entry.name: right
entry.summary: the right edge of the anchor rectangle

entry.name: on_demand
entry.summary: request regular keyboard focus on click

request.name: set_layer

description.summary: change the layer of the surface

request.description:
Change the layer that the surface is rendered on.
Layer is double-buffered, see wl_surface.commit.

arg.name: layer
arg.summary: layer to move this surface to
